title: Connected components as intersections of clopen neighbourhoods
statement: Let $T$ be a topological space satisfying the quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness and compact-open-basis conditions in [def-weil-spectral-space]: $T$ is quasi-compact, has a basis of quasi-compact open subsets, and the intersection of any two quasi-compact open subsets is quasi-compact. No sobriety assumption is imposed. For every $t\in T$, its connected component is $\bigcap\{V\subseteq T: V\text{ is open and closed and }t\in V\}$.

proof.text: Let $T_0$ be the connected component of $t$, and let $S=\bigcap_{\alpha\in A}Z_\alpha$, where $(Z_\alpha)$ lists all clopen subsets of $T$ containing $t$ (including $T$). The relatively clopen pieces $T_0\cap Z_\alpha$ and $T_0\setminus Z_\alpha$ separate $T_0$ unless the latter is empty, since the former contains $t$. Thus $T_0\subseteq S$.

The set $S$ is closed as an intersection of closed sets, and $t\in S$. If $S$ were disconnected, write $S=B\amalg C$ with $B,C$ nonempty and clopen in $S$. Being closed in the closed subspace $S$, they are closed in $T$, hence quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-in-quasi-compact].

Choose opens $O_B,O_C\subseteq T$ with $B=S\cap O_B$ and $C=S\cap O_C$. Cover $B$ by basis opens contained in $O_B$ and take a finite subcover, with union $U$. Then $B\subseteq U\subseteq O_B$, hence $B=S\cap U$. Cover $C$ by basis opens contained in $O_C$ and take a finite subcover with union $V$; then $C=S\cap V$. A finite union of quasi-compact subsets is quasi-compact: restrict an open cover to each subset and unite the finitely many finite subcovers. Thus $U,V$ are quasi-compact opens, $S\subseteq U\cup V$, and $U\cap V\cap S=\emptyset$.

By the intersection hypothesis, $K=U\cap V$ is quasi-compact. Since $K\cap S=\emptyset$, the relatively open sets $K\cap(T\setminus Z_\alpha)$ cover $K$. Take a finite subcover indexed by $F\subseteq A$. Put $Z'=\bigcap_{\alpha\in F}Z_\alpha$, with $Z'=T$ if $F=\emptyset$. Then $Z'$ is clopen, contains $t$, and $K\cap Z'=\emptyset$. This is the elementary finite-subcover argument of Tag 005D (lemma-intersection-closed-in-quasi-compact).

source.place: Tag 005F, proof, application of Tag 005D (lemma-intersection-closed-in-quasi-compact) to U intersection V

proof.text: The set $L=T\setminus(U\cup V)$ is closed in quasi-compact $T$, hence quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-in-quasi-compact]. Since $L\cap S=\emptyset$, the relatively open sets $L\cap(T\setminus Z_\alpha)$ cover $L$. A finite subcover indexed by $G\subseteq A$ gives $Z''=\bigcap_{\alpha\in G}Z_\alpha$ (equal to $T$ if $G=\emptyset$), clopen and containing $t$, with $L\cap Z''=\emptyset$. Thus $Z''\subseteq U\cup V$.

source.place: Tag 005F, proof, application of Tag 005D (lemma-intersection-closed-in-quasi-compact) to the complement of U union V

proof.text: Put $Z=Z'\cap Z''$. It is clopen, contains $t$, is contained in $U\cup V$, and avoids $U\cap V$. Hence $Z=(U\cap Z)\amalg(V\cap Z)$. Both pieces are open in $T$; their complements are respectively $(T\setminus Z)\cup(V\cap Z)$ and $(T\setminus Z)\cup(U\cap Z)$, also open. If $t\in B$, then $U\cap Z$ is a clopen neighbourhood of $t$, so $S\subseteq U\cap Z$ by definition of $S$. But $C=S\cap V$ and $U\cap V\cap S=\emptyset$, forcing $C=\emptyset$. If $t\in C$, then $V\cap Z$ is a clopen neighbourhood of $t$, so $S\subseteq V\cap Z$, forcing $B=S\cap U=\emptyset$. Both cases contradict nonemptiness. Thus $S$ is connected and contains $t$, so maximality of the connected component gives $S\subseteq T_0$. Together with step 1 this proves $S=T_0$.
